Each carries `submission`, the metadata workflows see as {{submission.*}} (reference, submitted_at, submitted_by, form { id, name, version }, source). Each item has status (queued, running, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled, none), status_label ("Waiting on Manager approval"), stages [{ node_id, name, assignees [{ id, name }], team, since, due_date }] (where the run is and who has it) and people (names). endpoints.description: The files on the task's Attachments tab, oldest first, with `can_add` (you can work on the open task), per-attachment `can_delete`, `legal_hold` (the task's form is held: nothing can be deleted), `type_suggestions` and `max_file_bytes`. Visible to the assignee, collaborators, team members, managers of an assignee, the assigner and holders of tasks.view_all / tasks.manage_queue; anyone else gets 404. Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.label: Attach a file to a task (or start a direct upload)
endpoints.description: You must be able to work on the open task (assignee, collaborator, team member, a manager of an assignee, tasks.complete_any, or tasks.manage_queue on a non-workflow task); needs a user-bound credential. With content_base64: the file is checked (size, type by content, blocked types, SVG sanitising, optional virus scan) and attached; returns `{ mode: "uploaded", attachment }`. With size only: `{ mode: "direct", attachment_id, upload: { url, method, headers }, expires_at }` — PUT the bytes to the URL with exactly those headers, then POST /tasks/{id}/attachments/{attachment_id}/complete — or `{ mode: "server", max_bytes }` when the storage can't sign uploads (send content_base64 instead). Requires tasks.complete.

endpoints.label: Finish a direct upload of a task attachment
endpoints.description: The uploader only, within the upload window (15 minutes by default), while they can still work on the task. The object is read back and verified; a file that fails is deleted and the reason returned. Requires tasks.complete.

endpoints.label: Delete a task attachment
endpoints.description: The uploader (while they can see the task) or a holder of tasks.delete. Refused (409) while the task's form is on legal hold. The attachment disappears at once; the stored file is purged after TASK_ATTACHMENT_DELETED_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.description: Returns `{ url, expires_at, attachment }`: a signed link valid for 5 minutes that needs no session (or the plain /attachments/<id> link, which needs a signed-in session, when the instance has no signing key). Every call is written to the audit log. Requires tasks.view_own.

Tasks shared with you (directly, through a team you are in or a role you hold) are listed without following them. Completed tasks stay until you unfollow them (hide_completed=true leaves them out); deleted tasks and tasks you can no longer see drop out. Personal: needs a credential bound to a user (tenant-wide keys get 403). Requires tasks.view_own.

endpoints.description: The task's invites, oldest first, and can_manage (whether you may invite and remove). Anyone who can see the task reads them; anyone else gets 404. endpoints.description: Shares the task, read only: everyone the invite names (directly, as a member of the team or a holder of the role) can open it (and its subtasks unless include_subtasks is false), its comments, attachments, history and process view, and comment. People invited directly follow it (Task tracker → Following) and get a notification and an email; members of an invited team or role get a notification when it has at most 25 people. Already-invited ones are left as they are. Recorded in the task history and the audit log. Invite and remove: the assignee or a collaborator, a member of the assigned team, the assigner, a manager of an assignee, a manager of the workflow, or tasks.complete_any (an invited viewer cannot invite others). Requires tasks.view_own.
